title.narrative: Emergency Response and Think Tanks Resilience Support 2022-2023
Nödåtgärder och stöd till tankesmedjors motståndskraft 2022-2023

description.narrative:
Support to Ukrainian think tanks seeks to contribute to Ukraines transformation into a successful, inclusive and accountable European democracy by creating conditions for independent public policy institutions to grow organizationally, strengthening the voice of independent think tanks in the policy process, making their output relevant for key stakeholder groups in the Ukrainian society, and enabling them to make a stronger impact on policy-making.
With the beginning of the war and full change of the playing field, the independent think tanks are facing (or will face in the future) the need to significantly refocus or adjust their activities to the new reality. They need to revisit their priorities, while maintaining contacts with their key stakeholders. The think tanks also need resources for rebuilding their teams, adjusting operations and policies, designing short- and medium-term solutions and products, and coping with stress.
A challenge today is maintaining the think tanks operational amid the high risk that think tanks may lose financing and be unable to keep their core teams, which in turn affect their capacity to remain relevant and serve their missions

Stöd till ukrainska tankesmedjor strävar efter att bidra till Ukrainas omvandling till en framgångsrik, inkluderande och ansvarsfull europeisk demokrati genom att skapa förutsättningar för oberoende offentliga politiska institutioner att växa organisatoriskt, stärka de oberoende tankesmedjornas röst i policyprocessen och göra deras resultat relevant för nyckel intressentgrupper i det ukrainska samhället och göra det möjligt för dem att göra en starkare inverkan på beslutsfattandet.
Med början av kriget och fullständig förändring av spelplanen står de oberoende tankesmedjorna inför (eller kommer att möta i framtiden) behovet av att avsevärt omfokusera eller anpassa sin verksamhet till den nya verkligheten. De måste se över sina prioriteringar, samtidigt som de upprätthåller kontakter med sina viktigaste intressenter. Tankesmedjorna behöver också resurser för att återuppbygga sina team, anpassa verksamhet och policyer, designa kort- och medellångsiktiga lösningar och produkter och hantera stress.
En utmaning idag är att upprätthålla tankesmedjorna i drift mitt i den höga risken att tankesmedjor kan förlora finansiering och inte kunna behålla sina kärnteam, vilket i sin tur påverkar deras förmåga att förbli relevanta och utföra sina uppdrag.

Support to Ukrainian think tanks seeks to contribute to Ukraine’s transformation into a successful, inclusive and accountable European democracy by creating conditions for independent public policy institutions to grow organizationally, strengthening the voice of independent think tanks in the policy process, making their output relevant for key stakeholder groups in the Ukrainian society, and enabling them to make a stronger impact on policy-making.
With the beginning of the war and full change of the playing field, the independent think tanks are facing (or will face in the future) the need to significantly refocus or adjust their activities to the new reality. They need to revisit their priorities, while maintaining contacts with their key stakeholders. The think tanks also need resources for rebuilding their teams, adjusting operations and policies, designing short- and medium-term solutions and products, and coping with stress.
A challenge today is maintaining the think tanks operational amid the high risk that think tanks may lose financing and be unable to keep their core teams, which in turn affect their capacity to remain relevant and serve their missions

The initiative is multi-faceted and has comprised a few elements, while the specific support during June 2022 July 2023 more of an emergency response to the needs of think tanks. It built on the premises, experience, and accomplishments of preceding support.
The demand for analytical products comes from various sources and stakeholders, like municipal governments, relevant ministries with whom selected think tanks have partnered, communities, or certain processes/developments (like the EU integration where some think tanks conduct monitoring of Ukraines fulfilment of EUs conditionalities for candidate status acquisition or compliance of Ukraine with acquis, etc.).
For instance, during the past months the following results could be highlighted:
- Co-organizing the conference "From Resilience to Recovery: the Critical Role for the Civil Society on September 29-30, 2022 in Kyiv and Lviv, which was attended by more than 200 representatives of civil society and the donor community. Eight representatives of partner think tanks participated in the conference as speakers/experts;
- Enhanced advocacy for meaningful engagement of think tanks, among other civil society actors, in shaping Ukraines reconstruction and recovery, and participation of think-tanks in the series of meetings related to the Ukraine Plan (Ukraine Facility) while providing expert proposals related to their sphere of competence to be included in the mentioned document. Representatives of partner think-tanks also participated in the Ukraine Recovery Conferences in Lugano (July 2022), Berlin (October 2022), London (June 2023) and the civil society side event by the Chatham House in June 2023. They have also engaged with the Ministry of Economy of Ukraine, the Ministry of Infrastructure, Communities and Territorial Development and the Agency for Restoration and Development of Infrastructure of Ukraine.
- Consultations and preparation of recommendations regarding the optimal model of support for think tanks and their involvement in the reconstruction process. Emergency grants were used to support 48 studies directed at overcoming the consequences of the war, reconstruction, and European integration of Ukraine.
Additional examples:
Most were desk studies that could be implemented within a 5-month grant. However, some of the partner organizations managed to conduct a survey and collect the necessary data for larger studies. Here are some examples of research carried out with TTDI support:
Center for Economic Strategy, Resilience of Economy to Security Challenges and its media coverage. The sectors of energy, logistics, financial sector, fiscal policy and international policy were analyzed and conclusions drawn about the sources of Ukraines stability during the wartime.
New Europe, Winter is coming: How to maintain Ukraines support by European societies? The note analyzes the following issues: what currently concerns Europeans in the context of the war; how much impact they have on supporting Ukraine; were the tools used by Russia to undermine Europes unity during the past 7 months effective, and do they have the potential to destabilize European societies in the future?
CEDOS, Politics of overcoming unemployment during war and post-war time; attitude of the population to state programs of socio-economic support and the need for them ; A year of full scale war in Ukraine: thoughts, feelings, actions.
The Sumy University Analytical Center completed the fourth wave of its survey of Social Resilience of territorial communities under the war-time conditions and a series of focus groups with local residents and internally displaced persons. The survey covered communities of Chernihiv, Kyiv, Lviv, Mykolayiv, Sumy and Zakarpattya regions and provided recommendations on access to basic social services, local governance and citizens engagement. The Pry-Carpathian University Analytical Center was able to continue producing its Analytical Radar that contributes to revising the Strategy of Development of Ivano-Frankivsk as the city that has hosted one of the largest numbers of IDPs. Social Resilience of territorial communities in conditions of the war time.
Centre for Society Research (CEDOS) - Analysis of data on the impact of the first year of full-scale war on society. Analysis of data on the impact of the war on the society, gathered in 2022 and early 2023, and also to analyse the dynamics of attitudes and adaptation of Ukrainians to social and economic challenges related to values, human relations, migration, conscription, mutual assistance. The funding was also used to produce and disseminate the research report, promote it through the online resources, national media and social networks. CEDOS updated the website to create a special project page and increase visibility of its key products, online courses and events.
TEXTY Data Journalism Agency enable the dynamic development of the think tanks information dashboard tracking and analysing the Russian propaganda in the time of the full-scale war, and to produce analytical reports on the dominating disinformation narratives to inform decision-making and work of the Ukraines Center for Countering Disinformation. With the additional funding, Texty engaged an external reviewer of its reports, hosted public events on disinformation (in Warsaw and online), organized a training for civil servants on recognizing and addressing disinformation during the war, enhanced communication of its analytical findings through social networks, and held a series of meetings with potential partners to design future joint projects. Texty also adapted its monitoring instruments, based on the use of digital, text and geo-space big data for anti-corruption, urban planning, finance tracking and other tools that can be used for monitoring reconstruction and European integration of Ukraine. Betrayal, panic, misinformation. What the fake telegram channels of the armed forces brigades write about.
VOX Ukraine enhance its Research on the hostile disinformation perception of Ukrainians. The extended funding was used to strengthen the think tanks prime countering disinformation tool, VoxCheck, and to lead a partnership work on the study of Ukrainians perceptions of narratives of the hostile disinformation. The study looked at how such narratives are perceived by Ukrainians of different demographic groups and locations and were presented to strategic communications counterparts in Ukraine and abroad. The study informed planning of future activities and products of VoxUkraine and helped expand the organizations contacts and international potential collaborations.
Analytical Center of the Ukrainian Catholic University (AC UCU) - Development of policy recommendations on compensation for war losses based on the methodology of an ethical tool for public policies. The funding enabled AC UCU to proceed with developing and disseminating an ethical approach to public policy making in the areas of post-war modernisation of Ukraine, focusing on policies of compensations and reparations of war damages. AC UCU designed an ethical policy analysis instrument in order to ensure that policy-making is rights-based. The funding will enable AC UCU to present the instrument in a visionary conference later in 2023, to expand a network of partners among key stakeholders, and strengthen its advocacy for the implementation of a right-based and values-based approach into reconstruction and recovery planning. Ethical reparations for war damages.
Come Back Alive despite being Ukraines most successful crowdfunding platform, the organization needs to make sure that its think tank arm continues to develop. The additional funding enabled Come Back Alive to complete its policy documents focusing on analysis of the civilian territorial defence in countering the full-scale russian aggression in early months since the invasion on 24 February 2022, and perspectives on the role of community-based territorial defence. The organization also enhanced its analysis of xenophobia in russia and the role of enforcement structures in the conservation of the current belarusian regime. Strengthening the analytical arm is instrumental to the organizations work on designing the future policies on veterans, their integration and overcoming the war aftermath. Generalization and assessment of experience of Territorial Defense Forces (TDF) application in 2022.
